title: Lightweight Cordless Vacuums Under $150 for Stiff Hands and Tired Arms: What the Listings Say
subtitle: A plain-English look at cordless stick and handheld vacuums, what they can and cannot do, and three Bissell models under $150 based on retailer listings.
excerpt: A cordless vacuum means no cord to plug in, but it also means short battery time and small dirt tanks. Here is what three Bissell models from about $45 to $145 list, based on the retailer's product pages, not hands-on testing.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Dragging a heavy upright vacuum out of the closet, unwinding the cord, finding an outlet and pushing the whole thing across the room can turn a quick tidy-up into a real chore. For anyone with stiff hands, a sore shoulder or simply less stamina than before, it is easy to put off.

A cordless vacuum skips the cord and the outlet hunt. The trade-off is that it runs on a battery for a limited time and holds less dirt. Here is what that means day to day, and three Bissell models under $150. One note up front: the details below come from the retailer's product pages (Abt). We have not tested these vacuums, and we did not find an independent review to rely on.
Stick or Handheld: What Is the Difference?
A stick vacuum is a slim, upright vacuum you push along the floor, a bit like a broom with a motor. Some models have a small hand vacuum that detaches from the main body for stairs and upholstery.
A handheld vacuum is a small unit you hold in one hand for spot jobs: crumbs on the counter, pet hair, a messy car. It is not meant for cleaning whole floors, and using one low down means bending.

The listings claim up to 12 to 20 minutes of runtime per charge and 3 to 4 hours to recharge. Those runtimes are the maker's best-case "up to" figures, and the ReadyClean's is footnoted with an asterisk. That is enough for a small flat or a few rooms, but not a whole house.
It also helps to know what these vacuums cannot do. None of the three mops, and they are not a good fit for large homes or thick carpet.

items: Weight you can actually hold. The ReadyClean stick vacuum lists 5.8 pounds, which is light for a stick vacuum but not feather-light, and that weight sits on your wrist when you use the hand vac or hold it up. The listings for the two handhelds did not give a weight, so do not assume they are lighter until you check.
Runtime that matches your home. Twelve to twenty minutes suits a small home or a few rooms, not a whole house.
Charging time. Expect 3 to 4 hours to recharge, so plan around that.
Emptying the dirt tank. The tanks are small and need emptying often. Emptying is a hand task that may be hard for arthritic hands, so ask whether you or a helper can do it comfortably.

Buttons and grip. The ReadyClean lists fingertip controls for suction level and brush roll on/off, but the product pages do not show whether the buttons and trigger are easy for stiff hands. Try one in person if you can.
How much you need to bend. Handhelds mean bending for floor-level jobs. The ReadyClean's 2-way folding handle is meant for reaching under furniture.
Ongoing costs. None of these lists a subscription or monthly fee. Battery replacement, filter costs and noise level were not confirmed, so check the maker's manual before you buy.
Warranty and returns. Each model lists a 1-year limited warranty. Read the seller's return policy, and note that Abt ships only within the contiguous US.

sections.content: Setting Up and Using It Well
Since runtime is short, it may help to clean in short sessions and give your arms a break between them. Remember that charging takes 3 to 4 hours.
Keep the manual handy. Abt links to each model's "Documents & Manuals" on the product page, which is the place to learn how to care for the filter and which replacement parts fit.
If you have arthritis or hand, shoulder or arm pain, ask your doctor or an occupational therapist about tools and techniques that suit you.

Shopping for a parent? Think about who will empty the dirt tank and how often. A lighter vacuum only helps if the person using it can also empty and recharge it without strain. If you can, visit a store together so they can hold it and try the controls before you buy.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A cordless vacuum will not replace every cleaning tool in the house, but for crumbs, pet hair and small jobs, it may take some of the effort out of tidying up. Pick the size that suits your home and your hands.

products.name: Bissell ReadyClean Cordless 10.8V Stick Vacuum (3190BB)
products.blurb: A stick vacuum listed for bare and sealed hard floors, low-pile carpet, rugs, stairs and pet beds. It lists 5.8 lb, up to 20 minutes of runtime, fingertip controls, a 2-way folding handle and a detachable hand vac with crevice and upholstery tools.

products.name: Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Lithium-Ion Cordless Hand Vacuum (2390)
products.blurb: A handheld listed for carpet, low-pile carpet, stairs, bare floors and pet beds. It has a powered head, 3 attachments, a 0.18 gal dirt tank and up to 17 minutes of runtime; the listing did not give a weight.

products.name: Bissell AeroSlim Cordless Handheld Vacuum (2986T)
products.blurb: A low-cost handheld listed for counter tops, car and garage. It offers up to 12 minutes of runtime and a 2-in-1 crevice tool and brush, though its 3.3 oz dirt capacity is small and no weight was listed.
